Use a neutral product description or the destination catalogue’s own listing identifier to narrow the results, then compare the current product page with your saved evidence. If you want the exact item from a Hacoo post, return to the official app or the verified original link; a visually similar catalogue result is only another candidate. Shipping and return policies discussed in this guide apply to orders made with the platform that issued those policies, not automatically to every external product route.

sections.heading: A repeatable search sequence
paragraphs: Write a five-field product brief. Search category plus one observable feature. Save no more than five plausible results with their identifiers and lead images. Verify every final destination, then build a three-candidate same-field shortlist. Reject mismatches and hard unknowns; do not fill missing details from a similar item. If search fails, vary one term, use the category route or search the exact code. Label unresolved or unavailable routes honestly. Before acting, repeat the image, identifier, option, measurement and current amount checks on the live destination. This sequence will not make every product discoverable, but it makes wrong clicks, stale links and unsupported claims easier to catch. The best product-search guide is not the one with the most links; it is the one that shows how each link earned a place.

hacoo-size-guide.title: Hacoo Size Guide: Shoes, Hoodies and Clothing Measurements
hacoo-size-guide.description: Choose Hacoo sizes with foot length, garment measurements, fit allowance and listing-specific evidence instead of relying on labels alone.
hacoo-size-guide.sourceNote: This independent measurement method was reviewed on 10 October 2026. Size charts and measurement methods are listing-specific; confirm the current option and instructions before ordering.

sections.heading: A size label is not a measurement
paragraphs: The same letter or number can describe different dimensions across product types, listings and regions. Begin with the current listing’s measurement information, not the size you usually buy. Record whether values describe the body, a flat garment, the inside of a shoe, the outsole or a recommended foot length. Units and endpoints matter: chest width is not chest circumference, and an outsole length is not usable interior space. If the method is not stated, mark it unclear. Never import a chart from a similar-looking listing. A useful Hacoo size guide does not announce that everything runs small or large; it teaches you to connect one exact option to comparable measurements and to make remaining uncertainty visible before ordering.

sections.heading: Measure an item that already fits
paragraphs: For clothing, choose a garment with the fit you want and lay it flat without stretching. Record shoulder seam to shoulder seam, chest width at a consistent underarm point, body length from the same neckline point, sleeve length with a stated start and any category-specific dimensions. Photograph the tape position for your private record. Measure twice and use the same units as the listing or convert once, clearly. The reference item is stronger than body memory because it captures ease and preferred silhouette. Do not mix a slim T-shirt reference with an oversized hoodie or compare a stretchy knit with rigid outerwear without noting the difference. Your goal is a repeatable baseline, not a claim that the two garments are constructed identically.

sections.heading: Use body measurements for the right fields
paragraphs: Body measurements can be useful when the listing explicitly maps them to a recommended size. Use a flexible tape, keep it level and measure over the clothing layer relevant to the intended use. Record the date, method and whether the value is body circumference. Avoid pulling the tape tight or adding an arbitrary number because an online rule says to ‘size up.’ Required ease depends on the product, fabric behavior and preferred fit. If the chart supplies finished-garment dimensions, compare those with a garment that fits rather than directly matching them to the body. Keep body data private; a simple range or reference garment is usually enough for a product note. Measurement evidence should improve the decision without exposing personal information.

sections.heading: Shoe sizing starts with foot length
paragraphs: Measure both feet late enough in the day to reflect normal expansion, wearing the sock type intended for the shoe. Stand on paper with weight distributed naturally, mark heel and longest toe, and measure the straight distance. Use the larger foot as the starting value. Then determine what the listing’s chart represents: recommended foot length, internal length, insole length or a regional size conversion. These values are not interchangeable. A shoe also needs width, toe shape and volume context; length alone cannot guarantee comfort. Do not add a universal allowance or select solely by an EU, UK or US label. Apply only the allowance or mapping supported by the current chart and category, and stop if the method remains ambiguous for a size-sensitive purchase.

sections.heading: Hoodies need layer and silhouette context
paragraphs: For a hoodie, chest width and body length usually matter more than the familiar letter label, while shoulder and sleeve measurements explain the silhouette. Measure a reference hoodie over the layer you expect to wear. Decide whether you want a close, regular or oversized result before comparing. A wider chest is not automatically better if body length, cuffs or shoulder drop become unsuitable. Note whether the listing measurement is flat width or circumference and whether any stated tolerance appears. Fabric composition or stretch should be recorded only when the current source states it; a photograph cannot establish recovery or shrinkage. If the chart omits a hard measurement, treat the size as unresolved rather than assuming the model photograph predicts your fit.

sections.heading: T-shirts, jackets and bottoms need different rows
paragraphs: A T-shirt comparison may prioritize chest, shoulder and body length. A jacket adds sleeve, closure, intended layers and sometimes hem width. Bottoms require waist method, rise, hip or thigh, inseam and leg opening, with special care over whether an elastic waist is measured relaxed or stretched. Do not compress these categories into one generic ‘true to size’ score. Build a small template for the item type and reject charts that omit a decisive field. For trousers, compare a flat reference garment using the same waist and inseam path. For outerwear, close zips or buttons before measuring when that matches the source method. Category-specific rows make a size guide actionable instead of repeating the unhelpful advice to check the chart.

sections.heading: Convert units without creating false precision
paragraphs: Use 2.54 centimetres per inch and keep enough precision for the tape and source, not a long decimal that implies laboratory accuracy. If the chart is rounded to whole centimetres, a conversion to hundredths of an inch does not improve the evidence. Label every value and retain the original unit beside the conversion. Check whether a range such as 52–54 describes product tolerance, body recommendation or different measurement methods. Do not average a range unless you are only using it as a rough midpoint and label that calculation clearly. A one-centimetre difference may be smaller than measurement variation, while a missing method can be more important than several centimetres. Precision begins with consistent endpoints and definitions, not extra digits.

sections.heading: Allow for tolerance without hiding a bad match
paragraphs: Manufactured garments and manual measurements can vary, and a listing may publish a tolerance. Use the stated tolerance when available; do not invent one. Compare the lowest and highest plausible values with your acceptable range. If the entire tolerance band works, the candidate is stronger. If only one edge works, fit risk is higher. A tolerance should not rescue a clear mismatch or replace a missing dimension. For footwear, measurement variation does not solve a width or toe-shape problem. For clothing, stretch shown in a photograph is not a quantified allowance. Write a decision such as ‘chest acceptable, sleeve unresolved’ instead of reducing every field to one average score. This preserves the reason a size might fail and makes alternatives easier to compare.

sections.heading: Read reviews as fit context, not a universal chart
paragraphs: A useful review states the exact option, relevant measurements, preferred fit and observed result. ‘Runs small’ without those details is weak evidence. Group comparable reports rather than counting every comment equally, and separate preference from product measurement. Someone who wanted an oversized hoodie may call a regular fit small; another person may prefer it. Never use a reviewer’s body details outside the context they chose to publish, and do not copy private photographs. Reviews can identify questions—narrow toe box, short sleeve, unclear waist stretch—but the current listing’s measurements and your reference item should remain central. If reviews conflict, record the uncertainty rather than selecting the most reassuring opinion.

sections.heading: Create a size decision table
paragraphs: Put the exact option in the first column, then list each hard measurement, source method, your reference value, acceptable range and result: pass, unknown or fail. Include the chart date and route because the same product page can change. Do not compare more than three candidates at once. A size can pass only if identity is stable and every non-negotiable field is supported. An unknown field may be acceptable for a loose accessory but not for fitted shoes or formal clothing. Avoid scoring that lets decorative strengths cancel a size failure. The table’s value is not mathematical sophistication; it is the discipline of evaluating every candidate through the same definitions and preserving why one option was chosen or rejected.

sections.heading: Recheck the selected option before ordering
paragraphs: Return to the live destination after making the table. Confirm the image, colour, exact size label, chart, unit and any option-specific note. Screenshots saved earlier are evidence of what you reviewed, not proof that the page is unchanged. Check the current amount and order-level delivery details separately from size. If the selected option changes automatically after navigating, reselect it and review the chart again. Save the final decision row and current date. This last check catches one of the easiest mistakes: measuring carefully and then ordering a different option from the one evaluated. It also creates a clean record of the information relied upon if the received item later needs to be measured.

sections.heading: Size-guide checklist
paragraphs: Identify whether the chart describes body, garment, foot, insole or outsole measurements. Measure a comparable item or both feet with recorded endpoints. Use the larger foot and relevant sock for shoes; use the intended layer and silhouette for clothing. Compare category-specific fields, keep units explicit and apply only a published tolerance. Treat reviews as context, never a replacement chart. Reject a candidate when a hard size field fails, and pause when the method or exact option is unclear. Reopen the destination and verify the selected size immediately before ordering. This process cannot promise fit, but it produces a far better decision than choosing by a familiar label or a generic instruction to size up.

hacoo-returns-refund-timeline.title: Hacoo Returns & Refunds: Deadlines, Evidence & Payment
hacoo-returns-refund-timeline.description: Prepare a Hacoo return or refund request with the official 15-day window, a clear evidence set and realistic review and payment stages.
hacoo-returns-refund-timeline.sourceNote: Official shipping information and the dedicated return/refund policy were checked on 10 October 2026. Published ranges are estimates. Eligibility and any physical return requirements depend on the current order-specific instructions; the two general pages use different return wording.

sections.heading: Start the clock from delivery
paragraphs: Hacoo’s official shipping information says after-sale support may be requested within 15 days of delivery, and its help material describes eligible-product return handling. Treat that window as a reason to inspect promptly, not a guarantee that every request will be approved. Save the recorded delivery date, the order reference, item and exact selected option. If an order arrives in several parcels, identify which delivery contains the affected item rather than using the first parcel date for everything. Recheck the current order-linked instructions because eligibility, exclusions and required steps can change. A general guide can explain how to prepare; it cannot extend a deadline or decide a case. Begin as soon as a material issue is identified instead of waiting for the end of the published window.

sections.heading: Classify the issue before gathering files
paragraphs: A wrong item, missing included part, visible damage, measurement discrepancy, unwanted eligible item and delivered-but-missing parcel are not the same case. Choose one primary issue and build evidence around it. Product mismatch begins with the live or saved listing, selected option and received item. Transit damage begins with the outer parcel, protective packaging and item condition. A missing parcel begins with the carrier’s delivered scan and location checks. Do not write a long narrative that mixes every dissatisfaction with shipping speed or support tone. A clear classification helps the official process request the right material and makes your desired resolution understandable. If two items have different issues, create separate evidence folders and follow the order workflow rather than combining them into one ambiguous complaint.

sections.heading: Preserve packaging and unedited evidence
paragraphs: If the parcel looks damaged, photograph all sides, the label and the affected area before opening. Record an unboxing sequence when practical, then photograph the item, included parts, size or option markings and the specific problem in neutral light. Keep original files with metadata and do not use filters, annotations that cover evidence or edits that remove context. A close-up should be paired with a wider image showing where the issue is located. Retain packaging, tags and accessories until the official instructions say what is required. Good evidence does not guarantee approval, but poor evidence can make a valid difference hard to understand. Store public and private copies separately so labels, names, addresses and order numbers are never exposed in a forum or review.

sections.heading: Describe observable differences
paragraphs: Replace conclusions such as ‘terrible quality’ with facts the reviewer can compare. State that a named accessory shown as included is absent, a seam is open at a measured location, the received colour differs from the selected option, or a garment measurement is a specified value using a documented method. For a measurement issue, show the tape from its starting point to endpoint and include the listing method when available. Avoid authenticity, material or safety claims that photographs cannot establish. If the issue depends on function, record the permitted test and result without causing additional damage. A short, structured description—expected, received, evidence file, requested outcome—is more actionable than emotional emphasis. Keep expectations tied to the exact option and information that existed when the order was placed.

sections.heading: Submit through the current official route
paragraphs: Open the affected order and use the available after-sale or support flow, or the current official contact route when directed. Verify the domain before entering order information. Follow the requested fields and file formats rather than sending evidence to unrelated social accounts. Save the submission time, case reference, selected reason, requested resolution and every file uploaded. Do not create duplicate cases unless official support instructs you to do so; multiple inconsistent descriptions can slow review. If the interface changes, document the route you used instead of relying on an old screenshot tutorial. An independent guide should never ask for your credentials or full evidence package. Its role is to help you prepare a concise record for the system that actually has authority to review the order.

sections.heading: Separate application review from refund settlement
paragraphs: The dedicated Hacoo return and refund policy describes application review within 24 hours, while noting that holidays or promotional periods can extend processing. Treat this as the published review expectation, not a universal promise and not a payment deadline. Check whether your case has actually been submitted, whether support has asked for evidence, and whether the reply approves a refund or merely confirms receipt of the request. Record the latest response and any order-specific next step. If the stated review period passes, follow up in the same case with its reference and submission timestamp rather than opening disconnected requests.

sections.heading: Return instructions come after eligibility review
paragraphs: Do not mail an item to an address found in an old post or search result. Wait for the current official instructions associated with the approved route. Record the return address or label, deadline, carrier method, packaging requirements and any reference that must be included. Photograph the item and sealed parcel before handoff, then keep the acceptance receipt and tracking record. Confirm whether several items belong in one parcel only when the instructions say so. An untracked self-arranged return can create a new evidence gap. The official process may distinguish free-return eligibility, exclusions and other situations, so avoid presenting one case as universal. Follow the directions for the exact item and order, and ask for clarification inside the case when an instruction is incomplete.

sections.heading: Track the return as a new custody chain
paragraphs: A return parcel needs its own timeline: label issued, parcel accepted, carrier movement, delivered to the instructed destination and acknowledged by the return system. Save the drop-off receipt and first physical carrier scan. If the carrier changes, retain both numbers. A delivered return scan can support proof of arrival, but it does not automatically mean inspection or refund completion occurred at the same moment. Record each stage separately. If tracking stalls, contact the active return carrier with its reference before making unsupported claims about the recipient. Keep labels private. This custody chain allows a later follow-up to answer a precise question—whether the parcel was accepted, received or reviewed—instead of treating the entire return as one invisible period.

sections.heading: Refund approval and payment settlement are different
paragraphs: Refund approval and receipt of funds are different stages. The dedicated policy lists 8–15 working days for credit-card refunds and 5–7 working days for PayPal. These are published estimates for those methods, not a guaranteed schedule for every order, region or payment route. Save the approved amount, currency, payment method and any refund-issued date or reference shown in your case. If only approval is visible, do not assume the payment-processing clock has already begun.

Compare your payment account with the confirmed refund record. A pending authorization, partial refund and completed credit are different entries. For a delay beyond the method-specific estimate, first establish whether the refund has been issued, then ask the payment provider to trace the supplied reference if necessary. Share financial details only through the provider’s private support route. A general guide cannot see the account or decide when a particular bank will post a transaction.

sections.heading: Respond to requests for more evidence
paragraphs: When a reviewer asks for another photograph or explanation, answer that request directly. Include the exact item, option and issue, then attach the clearest new evidence. Do not replace the original description with a different complaint because the first outcome feels uncertain. If the requested evidence cannot be produced—for example, packaging was discarded—say so accurately and provide the best remaining record. Preserve the question and your response. A useful follow-up may include a measurement retaken with the specified method, a wider view connecting a defect to the item, or the carrier case for a delivered-but-missing parcel. Avoid edited collages when original files are requested. Consistency and traceability make the case easier to assess even though they cannot determine eligibility.

sections.heading: Escalate with a one-page case summary
paragraphs: If the current published stage has passed without an update, prepare a summary with order and case references, affected item, delivery date, issue category, submission time, last official response, return tracking if applicable and one requested action. Attach only decisive files and refer to earlier evidence already in the case. Keep the tone factual. Do not threaten, speculate about motive or open unrelated channels that cannot access the order. If the question is payment settlement after approval, include the approval date and method; if it is return receipt, include the carrier delivery event. This summary helps the recipient see where the process stopped. It also protects you from rewriting the history differently on each contact.

sections.heading: Returns and refund checklist
paragraphs: Inspect each delivered parcel promptly and identify the exact item and option. Check the current 15-day after-sale wording and order-linked eligibility. Classify one primary issue, preserve packaging, create unedited evidence and describe observable differences. Submit through the current official route and save the case. Treat the published 24-hour review expectation, which may be extended during holidays or promotions, as request review rather than guaranteed bank settlement. Follow only the return instructions issued for the case, track the parcel as a new custody chain and separate approval from funds received. If a stage exceeds its current guidance, follow up with a compact timeline. This method cannot promise a refund, but it gives an eligible request the clearest, most private and most auditable presentation.

hacoo-shoe-qc-guide.title: Hacoo Shoe QC Guide: Shape, Soles, Stitching and Size Evidence
hacoo-shoe-qc-guide.description: Inspect Hacoo shoe photos in a repeatable order, from pair shape and sizing evidence to panels, soles, stitching and packaging.
hacoo-shoe-qc-guide.sourceNote: This independent visual-inspection method was reviewed on 10 October 2026. Photos cannot prove authenticity, comfort, exact materials or long-term durability.

sections.heading: Inspect the pair before the details
paragraphs: Begin with both shoes in one straight, well-lit frame. Confirm that the photograph belongs to the exact destination and selected option, then compare overall length, toe shape, heel height, collar opening and sole curve. A close-up of neat stitching cannot rescue a pair whose silhouettes visibly differ. Perspective can exaggerate one side, so use the most centred view and confirm concerns from another angle. Record ‘possible camera effect’ when the evidence is weak. Check whether left and right appear to be the same size and colour. The first QC decision is not whether a tiny detail is perfect; it is whether the pair has a coherent identity and broadly consistent shape worth examining further.

sections.heading: Confirm the size evidence
paragraphs: Read the listing’s measurement method before interpreting a ruler photo. Determine whether the value represents foot length, internal length, removable insole, outsole or a regional label. These values cannot be swapped. If an insole is measured, check that it lies flat, the tape starts at zero and the endpoint is visible. Compare with both feet and with a shoe that fits, using the intended sock. Length alone does not establish width, toe volume or comfort. Do not add a universal allowance that the chart does not support. If the exact option lacks usable measurement evidence, classify sizing as unresolved. A visually excellent shoe is still a poor candidate when the most consequential field cannot be connected to the selected size.

sections.heading: Check the toe boxes as mirrored shapes
paragraphs: Place an imaginary centre line through each shoe and compare toe width, height, taper and curvature. One toe may appear larger because it is closer to the camera, stuffed differently or rotated, so look for a second top or front view. Compare corresponding panel edges and the distance from lace row to sole. Minor hand-position or packing effects should not be labelled defects without confirmation. Look for dents, collapsed reinforcement, sharp asymmetry or a difference that persists across angles. The purpose is not to demand mathematical identity from soft materials; it is to identify shape differences likely to affect appearance or fit. Save the image and mark confidence as confirmed, likely or unresolved rather than forcing a yes-or-no claim.

sections.heading: Review panel alignment and symmetry
paragraphs: Follow major overlays and seams from the toe through the sides to the heel. Corresponding panels should begin and end in comparable positions, while allowing for camera angle and natural material movement. Check lace rows, eyelets, side panels, piping and any repeated decorative element. Use fixed references such as the sole edge or centre seam instead of the crop boundary. A slightly rotated shoe can make every line look uneven. If one feature appears displaced, ask whether the underlying shoe is angled before calling it misaligned. Record only visible construction; do not infer factory, batch or authenticity. Panel review is valuable because it links small details to the overall structure rather than judging an isolated stitch at extreme zoom.

sections.heading: Inspect the heel from straight behind
paragraphs: A rear view can show heel-counter alignment, collar height, centre seams, tabs and how the upper meets the sole. Prefer a photograph where both shoes stand on the same level surface. Compare vertical lines and the angle of each heel without using the edge of a tilted photo as a reference. Packing may compress a soft collar, while a persistent lean across views deserves attention. Check whether tabs or loops are centred and whether the seam reaches the sole consistently. A photograph cannot establish internal heel support or future comfort, so keep conclusions visual. If the heel is a hard requirement and no rear view exists, request better evidence where possible or leave the field unknown.

sections.heading: Trace stitching and edge finish
paragraphs: After shape passes, inspect primary stitch paths. Look for skipped sections, clusters of loose thread, abrupt spacing changes, puckering and ends that appear unsecured. Distinguish a loose surface fibre from a broken seam by checking a wider view. Along bonded edges, look for visible gaps, lifting or heavy residue, but remember that reflection and compression can imitate a mark. Use two angles before deciding. Do not describe glue strength, waterproofing or long-term seam durability from a still image. A QC note should name the location and evidence: ‘loose thread near left lateral eyelet in two views’ is more useful than ‘bad stitching.’ This specificity supports comparison and any later question without overstating what the photo proves.

sections.heading: Read the midsole and upper join
paragraphs: Scan the join around the full shoe where the upper meets the midsole. Check for a consistent edge, obvious gaps, deep dents, excess material or a section that appears lifted. Compare both shoes at equivalent locations. A decorative paint line or textured edge can look uneven in compressed images, so use the original-resolution view when available. The join’s appearance does not establish adhesion performance or durability. Do not bend, peel or perform a damaging test merely to create evidence. If a suspicious area is visible only in one low-quality frame, mark it unresolved and seek a clearer side view. The decision should reflect whether the uncertainty is acceptable for the intended use, not whether the photograph can be forced into certainty.

sections.heading: Compare outsole pattern and contact surface
paragraphs: A full outsole view should show that left and right patterns correspond to the selected model and option. Check for missing sections, large moulding defects, contamination, deep warping or an outsole attached in visibly different positions. Make sure dirt is not simply packaging dust and that lighting is not hiding a section. A tread photograph cannot guarantee grip on wet or slippery surfaces and should not be turned into a safety or performance claim. If the intended use requires a particular surface, record that requirement and whether the current listing states anything relevant. Visual texture is evidence of shape, not certified traction. Keep the outsole image connected to the same pair by matching size markings or the photo sequence where possible.

sections.heading: Check laces, hardware and included pieces
paragraphs: Confirm lace count, length consistency, eyelets, hooks, fasteners and any removable pieces shown as included for the exact option. A styled photograph may contain spare laces, charms or packaging that are not part of every selection. Use the listing text and option record, not the image alone, to decide inclusion. Look for damaged eyelets, missing hooks or mismatched hardware that is visible across views. For metal-like surfaces, report scratches or finish variation without claiming material composition. If a box matters, confirm whether it is explicitly included and inspect its condition separately from the shoes. Packaging condition may affect presentation, but it should not be confused with a construction assessment of the pair.

sections.heading: Evaluate colour and surface condition
paragraphs: Compare several views under similar lighting. White balance, exposure and reflections can shift colour, especially on glossy, metallic or textured surfaces. Use the displayed option name as the label and a neutral description for what is visible. Scan each shoe for stains, scuffs, pressure marks, scratches or inconsistent finish, then check whether the apparent mark moves with a reflection in another image. Do not assign an exact digital colour value unless a reliable source provides it. Material names and coating performance also require stated evidence. A useful note identifies location, image conditions and confidence: ‘dark mark on right outer panel appears in two angles’ is stronger than a general claim that the colour is wrong.

sections.heading: Know what shoe photos cannot prove
paragraphs: Photographs cannot reliably establish authenticity, odour, exact material composition, internal comfort, arch support, fit during walking, grip performance or long-term durability. They may be edited, compressed or captured before shipping conditions change the item. Do not turn a clean photo set into a quality guarantee. Instead, divide findings into visible pass, stated but not visually verified, and unresolved. Comfort and fit require personal context even when measurements are clear. If a seller or listing makes a performance claim, preserve the exact wording and source rather than adopting it as an independent conclusion. The honest limit of shoe QC is powerful: it can reject obvious mismatches and defects while exposing the remaining risks before a decision.

sections.heading: Shoe QC decision rule
paragraphs: Reject a candidate when the destination identity is unstable, pair shape differs materially across confirmed views, the exact size lacks essential evidence, or an unacceptable construction problem is clearly visible. Pause when camera angle, stuffing or lighting could explain the concern and another photograph can resolve it. Continue only when pair identity, overall silhouette, sizing method, panel alignment, heel, stitching, sole join, outsole and selected option are consistent with the intended use and your uncertainty tolerance. Save the identifier, date and decisive images. Recheck the live destination immediately before acting. This process does not authenticate footwear or promise performance; it creates a repeatable, evidence-led comparison that is much stronger than judging a logo close-up or one flattering hero image.

hacoo-clothing-qc-guide.title: Hacoo Clothing QC Guide: Fabric, Print, Seams and Measurements
hacoo-clothing-qc-guide.description: Review Hacoo clothing photos for silhouette, measurements, print placement, seams, closures and visible finish without unsupported material claims.
hacoo-clothing-qc-guide.sourceNote: This independent visual-inspection method was reviewed on 10 October 2026. Photos cannot prove exact fibre content, comfort, shrinkage, authenticity or long-term wear.

sections.heading: Begin with product identity and silhouette
paragraphs: Confirm that every QC image belongs to the same destination identifier, selected colour and size. Then inspect the full garment front and back before zooming. Compare shoulder line, body width, sleeve shape, hem, collar and overall proportion with the current listing. A garment can have tidy embroidery yet be the wrong cut or option. Make sure it hangs or lies in a way that allows comparison; folds, clips and model posture can distort the outline. Record whether the intended fit is close, regular or oversized so the review has a decision target. Do not infer fit from one styled photo. Identity and silhouette are the gate: if they are unclear, small-detail inspection cannot make the candidate reliable.

sections.heading: Verify measurements and their method
paragraphs: Read whether the chart gives body measurements, flat-garment widths or circumferences. For tops, prioritize chest, shoulder, body and sleeve length; for bottoms, waist method, rise, hip or thigh, inseam and leg opening; for jackets, include the layer and closure context. In measurement photos, check tape start, endpoint, flat placement and units. Compare with an owned garment measured the same way. Do not double a width unless the method supports using it as approximate circumference, and do not mix relaxed and stretched waist values. A size label is not evidence of dimension. If a hard measurement is missing or the selected option uses another chart, record the field as unresolved and avoid the generic advice to size up.

sections.heading: Inspect the garment on a straight reference
paragraphs: Use a centred flat-lay, hanger or neutral model view to compare left and right. Check shoulder height, sleeve length, side seams, pocket position and hem line. A rotated photograph or uneven surface can create false asymmetry, so confirm with another view. For bottoms, compare leg width and seam path; for zip garments, close the zip when judging centre alignment if a closed view exists. Soft fabric will not form a perfect geometric shape, and normal drape should not be called a defect. Look for differences that persist across images or are anchored to construction points. The purpose is to identify a twisted panel, noticeably uneven component or mismatched cut, not to demand rigid symmetry from flexible cloth.

sections.heading: Read fabric appearance without inventing composition
paragraphs: Photographs can show surface texture, knit or weave visibility, drape, thickness cues and possible transparency under the photographed conditions. They cannot reliably prove fibre percentages, softness, breathability, waterproofing, warmth, stretch recovery or shrinkage. Copy any stated composition accurately and note which part it covers—shell, lining, filling or trim. Keep marketing phrases such as ‘premium’ or ‘cotton feel’ separate from formal composition. Compare close-ups with wider views because compression and sharpening can exaggerate texture. If opacity matters, look for multiple lighting conditions but do not call the garment opaque in all use. A responsible QC record has three columns: stated material information, visible surface evidence and performance questions that remain unanswered.

sections.heading: Trace structural seams
paragraphs: Follow shoulder, armhole, side, crotch, inseam and pocket seams from end to end depending on category. Look for skipped stitches, loose-thread clusters, puckering, open sections or abrupt changes in spacing. Inspect high-stress junctions and bar tacks where visible. A stray thread does not necessarily mean the seam is open, so use a wider image to understand the structure. For lined garments, check whether the lining sits smoothly at openings without claiming how it will behave in wear. Name the exact location of any concern and compare both sides. Still photos cannot establish seam strength or durability; they can show visible construction that deserves acceptance, rejection or a request for clearer evidence.

sections.heading: Check prints, embroidery and appliqué placement
paragraphs: Judge placement relative to the garment’s centre, neckline, pockets and seams rather than the crop. Compare front and back and check whether a fold is shifting the design. For prints, look for missing areas, obvious cracking, colour bleed or edge lifting visible at normal scale. For embroidery, inspect outline consistency, loose threads and whether the fabric puckers around dense areas. Extreme zoom can make normal stitch variation look dramatic, so pair details with a full-garment view. A photograph cannot promise wash resistance or long-term adhesion. Avoid brand-authenticity conclusions based on logo shape alone. The useful question is whether the visible execution and alignment meet the buyer’s requirement for this exact garment and option.

sections.heading: Review collars, cuffs and hems
paragraphs: These edges strongly affect shape. Check whether a collar lies evenly, ribbing width is consistent, cuffs match and hems appear straight without twisting. Compare left and right sleeve openings and inspect the junctions where ribbing meets the body. Packaging folds can temporarily distort soft edges, so look across several images before deciding. For drawcord garments, compare exit positions and cord length while recognizing that styling can move the cords. Do not claim elastic recovery or future stretching from appearance. If a neckline dimension matters, include it in the specification record rather than relying on a model photograph. Edge review should connect visible construction to the preferred silhouette, not turn every wrinkle into a defect.

sections.heading: Test closure and pocket evidence conservatively
paragraphs: Confirm the number and position of zips, buttons, snaps, pockets and adjustment points against the exact option. A still image may show that a closure exists and is aligned, but it cannot prove smooth operation. Check whether teeth or tracks look straight, buttons correspond to holes, snaps sit evenly and pocket openings match. For cargo or jacket pockets, distinguish decorative flaps from clearly usable openings. Do not infer pocket depth or carrying capacity without dimensions or a reliable demonstration. If a functional feature is essential, request or find evidence that directly addresses it. Record presence, visible condition and unknown performance separately. This prevents a polished photograph from silently becoming a guarantee that every feature works as imagined.

sections.heading: Compare colour under more than one image
paragraphs: Use the selected colour name, then compare front, back and close-up views for consistency. Screen settings, white balance, reflections and editing can alter colour. For a coordinated outfit or uniform, define an acceptable range before deciding. Look for isolated stains, dye marks or inconsistent panels, and confirm whether an apparent change follows a shadow or fold. Avoid assigning a precise colour code from a photograph. Prints and fabric may reflect light differently even when they belong to the same option. If the listing uses several styled images, make sure they all represent the selected variant. Colour QC is strongest when it reports repeated visible differences and weakest when it treats one saturated promotional image as a calibrated reference.

sections.heading: Check included pieces and option boundaries
paragraphs: A styled outfit may show trousers, accessories or layered garments that are not included. Record the exact option text, quantity and any explicitly listed pieces. For sets, confirm each component and the size relationship if stated. Check detachable hoods, belts, straps, spare buttons or patches only when the source indicates inclusion. An image containing several items is not sufficient evidence that all are supplied. If quantity or bundle contents are unclear, make that a pre-decision question. This check prevents a visual merchandising choice from becoming an unsupported expectation. It also helps on delivery because the saved option and included-piece record can be compared with the received contents without relying on memory.

sections.heading: Know the limits of clothing photos
paragraphs: Images cannot reliably establish authenticity, exact composition, odour, skin feel, comfort, thermal performance, waterproofing, colourfastness, shrinkage or long-term durability. Model photographs also cannot predict fit without relevant measurements and context. A strong QC conclusion therefore uses confidence labels: visible across several clear views, stated by the current source, likely but unconfirmed, or unresolved. Do not use an attractive close-up to upgrade a marketing phrase into a technical fact. If care or performance is important, look for explicit current information and preserve its wording. Visual QC is valuable because it can catch mismatches and construction concerns early, but it should make the remaining uncertainty clearer rather than hiding it behind a total quality score.

sections.heading: Clothing QC decision rule
paragraphs: Reject a candidate when identity or option is unclear, decisive measurements fail, an unacceptable construction problem appears across reliable views, or bundle contents do not match the requirement. Pause when folds, lighting or camera angle could explain a concern and better evidence may resolve it. Continue only when silhouette, measurements, seams, print or embroidery, edges, closures, colour and included pieces are consistent enough for the intended use. Save the destination ID, selected option, date, measurement method and decisive images. Reopen the current destination immediately before acting. This process cannot guarantee fit or wear, but it produces a transparent decision that is far stronger than judging a cropped model image, a familiar size label or an unsupported ‘true to size’ claim.

hacoo-links-not-working.title: Hacoo Links Not Working: Recover or Replace a Broken Listing
hacoo-links-not-working.description: Fix a Hacoo link that opens an error, the app home screen or the wrong product. Check the address, recover the listing and verify any replacement.
hacoo-links-not-working.sourceNote: Official Hacoo platform and contact information checked on 10 October 2026. The link-recovery method is independent editorial guidance; it does not establish why a particular listing disappeared or promise that it can be restored.

sections.heading: Identify the failure before changing your search
paragraphs: When Hacoo links are not working, start by naming the visible failure. A browser error, an app opening at its home screen, a missing product page, an unavailable size and a page showing another item are different problems. Write down the exact message and the final destination. This takes less time than repeatedly opening the same address and gives the next check a purpose. Do not assume every failed route means the product has sold out.

This guide addresses a previously saved link that no longer reaches the expected listing. If you never had a specific destination, begin with the broader product-finding guide. Here, success means recovering a verifiable listing or recording a clear reason to retire the old link. A replacement that merely looks similar is a new candidate, not a confirmed recovery.

sections.heading: Preserve the original address and product clues
paragraphs: Before editing anything, save the complete original address in a private note. Add where you found it, when it last worked if known, the expected category, the visible product title and any listing identifier. Keep a screenshot of the earlier product card if you already have one. Do not overwrite the source with a guessed correction; you may need to compare the two later.

Give the saved item a short identity description based on observable details: cream low-top shoe, dark heel panel, textured sole, size option recorded. This is more useful than a promotional caption. Separate what you actually saved from what you remember. If no identifier or clear image survives, label the identity uncertain before searching. That prevents a convincing alternative from quietly becoming the supposed original.

sections.heading: Check whether copying damaged the address
paragraphs: Compare the address in your note with the clickable source. A message may show shortened text while hiding a longer destination. Copied punctuation, an incomplete path or a line break can change what opens. Use the source's copy-link control when one is available, then inspect the resulting address before retrying. Preserve any meaningful product identifier rather than reconstructing a route from memory.

If the original source is gone, do not add random letters or swap domains until something loads. Record that the address cannot be verified. A working home page at a similar-looking address does not establish a connection to your item. Equally, a route containing an affiliate or sharing parameter is not automatically damaged. The useful test is whether the complete saved destination consistently reaches the expected content.

sections.heading: Compare browser and app behaviour once
paragraphs: Open the verified link in your normal browser and note the result. If it offers an app route, compare what happens there. Record whether you arrive at the same product, a general feed, a sign-in screen or an error. An app opening successfully is only one step: the product identity still needs to survive the handoff. Returning to the home screen does not prove that the listing has been deleted.

Check for an available update through your device's normal app store if the installed app is outdated. Keep the account and regional context consistent during the comparison. Avoid changing several settings together, because you then cannot tell which change affected the result. Do not delete saved data merely to test one broken link. If browser and app show different outcomes, retain both observations for support.

sections.heading: Separate a missing page from an unavailable option
paragraphs: When a page loads, read its current state before abandoning it. The entire listing may be unavailable, or only the previously selected size, colour or bundle may be missing. Check the product identifier and option labels. A title and image still appearing on screen do not establish that your particular option can be ordered. Likewise, an inactive option does not prove that every variation has disappeared.

Write a precise result such as page visible, blue medium unavailable, other options not assessed. If a different size is offered, assess it using current measurements instead of treating it as an automatic substitute. A changed bundle also needs a fresh quantity and contents check. Keeping page availability separate from option availability makes your saved list more accurate and avoids replacing a useful link unnecessarily.

sections.heading: Treat a wrong destination as a failed link
paragraphs: A link can load perfectly and still fail its purpose. Compare the destination's identifier, lead image, silhouette, colour layout and selected option with your saved evidence. If the route now shows a category, an unrelated item or a generic search page, mark it as redirected or mismatched. Do not keep the old product name above a new destination merely because the button still works.

For a visually close result, look for distinguishing details: the number of pockets, seam placement, fastening type, sole shape or strap attachment. One shared photograph is weak evidence when other fields differ. Record disagreements explicitly. A recovered listing should match the identity you can substantiate; any unresolved conflict belongs in the decision, not hidden in a footnote beneath an unchanged card.

sections.heading: Recover a candidate using the strongest saved clue
paragraphs: Start with the exact listing identifier if the current search interface supports it. Then try the preserved title or a short combination of category and distinctive features. Change one clue at a time so you know what produced each result. Keep recovered candidates in a separate list from the original record. Searching is a discovery step; the result becomes a recovery only after identity checks pass.

Limit the comparison to a few plausible candidates. For each one, record the current address, identifier, matching details and conflicting details. If none retains the original identifier, describe the outcome as an alternative found unless stronger evidence connects the records. Do not imply that the platform restored a listing simply because you discovered a similar item. That distinction matters when prices, measurements or included pieces have changed.

sections.heading: Use an old screenshot as a comparison aid
paragraphs: An old screenshot can preserve details that a dead address no longer reveals. Extract visible text, category clues, the product identifier and distinctive construction features. Crop a private copy to the useful product area when comparing images, while retaining the original for context. Avoid treating a prominent brand-like phrase or a familiar photograph as proof that two listings are identical.

Compare the screenshot against several views of each candidate. A matching front image can conceal different dimensions, lining, hardware or options. Where the screenshot shows a price or stock notice, treat it as historical evidence only. The current destination must supply the present terms. If the old image is too small to establish a decisive feature, write that limitation down instead of increasing confidence through repeated visual similarity.

sections.heading: Keep region and account messages in their proper context
paragraphs: If the page explicitly mentions a region or account restriction, preserve the wording. Confirm that the account reflects your actual country and that you are checking the intended language route. A page failing under one context does not prove universal unavailability. Conversely, seeing a listing through another context does not establish that it can be ordered or delivered under yours.

Do not use a different country setting simply to make an unavailable button appear. The relevant question is whether the listing and option are supported for your actual purchase circumstances. Where the interface does not explain the restriction, use official support with the saved address and error text. This independent index cannot unlock regional availability, change account permissions or verify an order on your behalf.

sections.heading: Repair saved spreadsheets without hiding the change
paragraphs: If you maintain a Hacoo spreadsheet or bookmark collection, preserve the old address in a history field and add a current status. Useful statuses include recovered, option unavailable, destination changed, temporary error observed and no verified replacement. Add the date of the check. A dated status lets readers distinguish a maintained record from an unexplained link swap.

For a verified replacement, update the image, title, identifier and option notes together. Recheck measurements and any displayed price rather than carrying them across from the retired row. When the candidate is only an alternative, say so clearly. Remove a purchase-facing button if the underlying product cannot be verified; the descriptive record can remain useful without sending readers into a misleading destination.

sections.heading: Finish with a recorded outcome and a current check
paragraphs: Stop troubleshooting when you can state one clear outcome. The original listing works again; the listing works but the desired option does not; a different candidate is available; or no reliable route remains. Each outcome supports a different next step. Only the first represents full recovery, and it still requires a final check of the current option and product information.

Use the catalogue search or a relevant category to assess an alternative when recovery fails. Keep that new comparison separate from any existing order: a broken discovery link does not cancel a purchase or explain a delivery issue. For an order problem, use the order record and its support route. A careful stop point saves time and keeps the independent guide accurate even when the original product cannot be found.

hacoo-tracking-not-updating.title: Hacoo Tracking Not Updating: Check the Gap and Next Step
hacoo-tracking-not-updating.description: Work out why Hacoo tracking appears stuck: separate label creation, physical scans, carrier handoffs and missed estimates before contacting support.
hacoo-tracking-not-updating.sourceNote: Hacoo shipping and contact guidance checked on 10 October 2026. The diagnostic examples are illustrative, not reports of tested orders. Scan gaps alone do not establish a cause, loss or a guaranteed delivery date.

sections.heading: Capture the unchanged event before refreshing again
paragraphs: If Hacoo tracking is not updating, record the last event before deciding what it means. Open the relevant order, identify the parcel and save the exact status, displayed event time, location and carrier. Also note the time you checked. Reopening the same screen without recording those details makes a quiet period feel longer while adding little useful information.

Look first for an explicit request that needs action, a failed delivery attempt or a delivered status. Those states need their own response and should not be treated as a routine scan gap. If the screen simply shows no newer movement, continue with the checks below. The purpose is to identify the missing evidence and the right next question, not to assign a cause from silence.

sections.heading: Build two clocks for one parcel
paragraphs: Keep an order clock and a movement clock. The order clock starts with the recorded purchase and includes any processing period. The movement clock starts with a physical carrier event when one is visible. Write both dates alongside the latest estimate shown for the purchase. A parcel with no acceptance scan presents a different question from one that was accepted and then stopped showing progress.

Avoid counting from a notification you cannot identify. An email saying that an order is being prepared, a label timestamp and an arrival at a sorting facility are not interchangeable milestones. If a field is absent, mark it missing. A simple two-clock note prevents you from describing several days of preparation as several days spent in the carrier network without evidence.

sections.heading: Read label creation as a limited observation
paragraphs: A tracking number or an electronic-information status gives you a reference to follow. On its own, it does not establish that the parcel has physically entered a carrier's custody. Read the exact wording instead of mentally upgrading label created to parcel moving. If no acceptance or collection event is visible, make that the unresolved point in your notes.

Check whether the order page provides a processing update or a separate dispatch message. If the relevant estimate has passed, ask support whether collection occurred and which event confirms it. Do not invent a warehouse location from the label or assume a particular delay cause. Keeping the observation narrow produces a more answerable support request than stating that a parcel is lost before any physical scan is available.

sections.heading: Find the last event that actually shows movement
paragraphs: When several tracking entries repeat similar wording, work backwards to the last event that adds meaningful information. A new timestamp attached to a general in-transit message may not show a new location or handoff. Record what changed: facility, carrier, destination stage or delivery attempt. Keep the original wording beside your plain-language interpretation so the two do not become confused.

Compare the elapsed period with the specific route and estimate available in the order. Do not turn an internet anecdote into a rule that every parcel must scan daily. Your evidence may support only that no newer event is visible. It does not, by itself, distinguish transport time, delayed data exchange, a missed scan or a parcel problem. Those remain possibilities until an official record clarifies them.

sections.heading: Reconcile app and carrier timestamps
paragraphs: Use the carrier information attached to the order to inspect the relevant carrier record, when available. Compare the tracking number character by character before comparing statuses. Then record the event date, time and any stated timezone on both screens. A notification arriving today can describe yesterday's event; an app check time is not necessarily the time the parcel moved.

If the two views differ, preserve both instead of choosing the more reassuring one. Write a short comparison: carrier shows a sorting event dated Tuesday; order view still shows Monday's handoff. Do not infer which system is wrong unless the source explains the mismatch. If one source adds a collection instruction or other required action, follow that official instruction while retaining the discrepancy in your case notes.

sections.heading: Check whether the parcel changed carriers
paragraphs: A delivery can involve more than one carrier reference. Inspect the order's logistics details for a local delivery number or named handoff. Follow a second number only when the order or carrier record connects it to your parcel. A search engine result for a similar number is not enough. Keep the original and local references together so later messages remain traceable.

If the first carrier shows a handoff while the next carrier shows no physical receipt, record that gap precisely. Ask which party can confirm acceptance at the next stage. Do not assume that a handoff message guarantees a delivery attempt the following day. The useful distinction is between a documented change in responsibility and a guessed schedule based on what happened to someone else's order.

sections.heading: Map each ordered item to its parcel
paragraphs: Before reporting that an entire Hacoo order is stuck, check whether its items are assigned to separate parcels. Create one row for each tracking number, then list the item lines it covers. Mark any item whose parcel assignment is unclear. This makes it possible to discuss the delayed portion without treating a delivered parcel as evidence that every item has arrived.

Hacoo's shipping guidance describes separate dispatches for available items and preordered or backordered items. Your own order record still needs to establish the actual split. If a parcel has arrived, compare its contents with the corresponding item lines. An unassigned item, an unopened second parcel and a missing item from an expected parcel are different cases and should be described separately to support.

sections.heading: Compare the gap with the purchase estimate
paragraphs: Record the delivery estimate currently attached to the order and any earlier estimate you saved. Note whether it is a date, a range or a business-day statement. Do not add a broad country range on top of an order-specific receiving estimate unless the interface says to do so. That can double count time and obscure whether the stated window has actually passed.

Hacoo's public shipping page treats delivery times as guidance rather than guaranteed dates. It does not provide a universal rule for how often every parcel must scan. If the purchase estimate has passed, ask for a parcel-specific update instead of resetting your wait to another generic range. If it has not passed, an explicit exception or required action can still justify contacting the relevant official support route.

sections.heading: Respond to a specific exception, not an imagined cause
paragraphs: An exception message changes the next step because it supplies more information than silence. Copy the exact text and any instruction, deadline or contact route that accompanies it. An address query calls for an address check; an attempted-delivery notice calls for reviewing the carrier's delivery options. A customs-related message needs the details actually provided for that parcel, not assumptions based on the destination country.

When the wording is unclear, ask what action is required and who needs to take it. Do not submit speculative explanations such as the parcel must be seized or stolen. Those claims can distract from the visible issue. Keep the unresolved question concrete: whether an address field is missing, whether a collection is available, or whether a requested document has been received.

sections.heading: Send one support message with a usable timeline
paragraphs: A useful message includes the order reference, parcel reference, last meaningful scan, date checked, displayed delivery estimate and the question you need answered. Supply private order details only through the appropriate support channel. Keep a copy of the message and case number. If you contact a carrier and Hacoo, cross-reference the existing case so each can understand what has already been checked.

For an illustrative parcel, the message could read: The order shows carrier acceptance on Monday and no later event when checked on Friday. Its displayed delivery window ends Saturday. The carrier page shows the same status. Please confirm whether a later physical scan is available and whether I need to take any action. Replace every example detail with your own record; this is a format, not a prediction about delivery.

sections.heading: Recheck against the response and close the correct case
paragraphs: Use the next update time supplied by support or the carrier to plan a recheck. If none is supplied, ask when to follow up and which reference to use. Avoid creating a new unrelated ticket each time you refresh. Add new events to the existing timeline, retaining the earlier evidence so the duration of the gap remains clear.

When tracking resumes, confirm that the update belongs to the same parcel and actually answers the unresolved question. When it changes to delivered, verify receipt and item coverage rather than closing the case automatically. If a parcel remains missing after a delivered scan, move to the delivered-but-not-received guide. A tracking gap is resolved by new evidence or a documented support outcome, not by a more optimistic guess.

hacoo-delivered-but-not-received.title: Hacoo Delivered but Not Received: Find and Report the Parcel
hacoo-delivered-but-not-received.description: Check a Hacoo parcel marked delivered but missing: match the tracking number, inspect delivery evidence and prepare a clear carrier and support report.
keywords: Hacoo package says delivered but not here
hacoo-delivered-but-not-received.sourceNote: Official shipping, contact and return/refund pages checked on 10 October 2026. This is independent evidence-organising guidance. A delivered scan does not determine a support outcome, and order-specific instructions govern the available next steps.

sections.heading: Confirm which parcel the delivered status covers
paragraphs: If Hacoo says delivered but you have not received the parcel, begin with the exact order and tracking number. Check that the delivered event belongs to the missing parcel and that the items you expected were assigned to it. A notification can be easy to confuse with another order, particularly when several parcels are moving at the same time.

Write down the item lines, parcel reference and carrier shown in the order. If one order has several tracking numbers, separate them before doing anything else. A delivered parcel may contain only part of the purchase. The immediate problem is to establish what is missing: a whole parcel, another parcel still in transit, or an item absent from a parcel that you did receive. Each requires different evidence.

sections.heading: Save the delivered event while details are visible
paragraphs: Capture the exact delivered wording, event date and time, location description and carrier name. Note when you checked the screen and whether the displayed timezone is stated. Save any associated photograph, signature field or delivery note through the available interface. Retain the full context privately; a cropped status word without its tracking reference is less useful when several cases are being compared.

Keep observations separate from conclusions. The record may show left in a designated place, handed to a named recipient, or simply delivered with no further detail. Those are different levels of evidence. Do not rewrite a vague event as proof that someone signed or that a particular address was visited. Your first report should accurately describe what the record shows and what remains unknown.

sections.heading: Check the likely handoff locations methodically
paragraphs: Review any delivery instructions you provided and check the locations you can normally access: the usual parcel area, reception desk, building mailroom or a designated collection point mentioned in the record. Ask household members or authorised recipients whether they accepted it. If a neighbour or reception service is specifically named, check that lead without assuming that every nearby address is involved.

Record what you checked and the time, including a negative result. A short note such as reception checked at 18:00, no parcel recorded gives the next person a concrete starting point. Avoid searching indefinitely while postponing a report. If the delivery evidence points to an unfamiliar location or you cannot access the indicated place, explain that limitation to the carrier instead of treating the search as complete.

sections.heading: Compare the address with the order record
paragraphs: Open the delivery address stored against the purchase and compare it with the intended destination. Check the house or building number, flat or unit, postcode and recipient details. A current account address may differ from the address used when the order was placed, so inspect the actual order record. Note any difference without altering your saved evidence of what was originally submitted.

If you find an error, explain precisely which field differs when contacting support. Do not assume that editing your profile after delivery will redirect the parcel or amend the completed record. If the order address is correct, say that you checked it. This removes a basic uncertainty while leaving the carrier to establish where the parcel was actually handed over.

sections.heading: Read proof of delivery without overstating it
paragraphs: When a photograph is available, compare stable features such as the doorway, floor pattern, parcel area and visible building details. A close-up of packaging may confirm that a parcel was photographed without identifying the location. A familiar-looking entrance may still be ambiguous in a building with repeated layouts. Describe the specific match or mismatch rather than asserting a location that the image cannot establish.

For a signature or recipient field, record what appears and whether you recognise it. Ask the carrier to clarify unclear evidence using its normal investigation process. Do not publish the image or another person's details as an accusation. Keep the useful issue narrow: the photograph does not show the expected entrance, the named recipient is unknown, or no location evidence is available in the record.

sections.heading: Contact the carrier responsible for the delivered scan
paragraphs: Hacoo's shipping page directs users with a delivered-but-missing parcel to the relevant carrier using the tracking information. Start from the carrier details linked to your order. Provide the tracking reference, delivered event, address check, local checks and any mismatch in the delivery evidence. Ask the carrier to investigate the handoff and confirm the next step for your case.

Request a case reference and the expected response or follow-up time. Save the response in the same timeline as your screenshots. If the carrier says only the sender can open the required investigation, retain that instruction and pass it to Hacoo support. Do not represent the carrier's refusal to discuss a case as proof of parcel loss; it may instead identify who must initiate the next process.

sections.heading: Give Hacoo support the carrier evidence
paragraphs: Use the support route available through your actual order or the official contact information. Explain that the parcel is marked delivered but has not been located, then attach the carrier case reference and a short account of the checks completed. If you have contacted the carrier but received no useful response yet, state that clearly rather than filling the gap with an assumed outcome.

Ask what additional evidence is required, which party is handling the investigation and when to follow up. Keep any order-level application or case number beside the carrier reference. Hacoos Shop is an independent guide and cannot inspect your account or decide a claim. Product search pages and catalogue contact forms should not substitute for the support channel attached to the purchase.

sections.heading: Separate a missing parcel from missing contents
paragraphs: If you receive a parcel but one item is absent, preserve the packaging and check the order's parcel assignments before describing the problem. Compare the label reference, packing information when present and the items actually received. Another tracking number may account for the outstanding item; if it does not, the issue concerns the contents of a received parcel rather than an entirely missing delivery.

Record condition details that you can observe, such as an open seam, damaged packaging or an item-count discrepancy. Do not infer who caused the problem from packaging alone. Use clear photographs and an item-by-item account when the support process requests them. Distinguishing these cases helps you supply relevant evidence and prevents the delivered scan from being treated as an answer to a different problem.

sections.heading: Use a concise report that can be followed
paragraphs: An effective report starts with the unresolved issue, then presents the evidence in time order. Include the order and parcel references privately, the displayed delivery time, the address check, the delivery evidence and the locations or recipients already checked. Finish with the carrier reference and a specific request, such as confirmation of the handoff location or initiation of the investigation that the carrier requires.

An illustrative summary is: Tracking marks this parcel delivered on Wednesday at 14:20. The order address is correct. No one in the household or reception has received it. The photograph does not show our usual entrance. Carrier case A is open. Please confirm what evidence is needed and whether a sender investigation is required. Replace these details with the actual record; do not copy a mismatch that you have not observed.

sections.heading: Record support deadlines without assuming a refund
paragraphs: Report the issue promptly and keep every deadline shown by the order or support team. Hacoo's public shipping page mentions a 15-day after-sales window after delivery, while its return policy describes case-dependent instructions. Neither statement should be converted into a promise that a missing-parcel report automatically produces a refund. Ask how the recorded delivery date affects the steps available for your specific case.

Separate investigation, application review, any approved remedy and the eventual payment outcome in your notes. They are different stages. Do not send goods to an address found in a general article or assume that a return is required for a parcel you never received. Follow the written instructions attached to the case and preserve the response that explains the next action and responsible party.

sections.heading: Close the timeline only after the outcome is clear
paragraphs: If the parcel is found, record where and when it was received and check that its contents match the relevant item lines. Update the open carrier and Hacoo cases through their normal channels so the record reflects the outcome. Finding one parcel does not close a separate missing-item or second-parcel issue; keep those records distinct until their own facts are resolved.

If the parcel remains missing, follow up using the existing case number and the next date provided. Add new evidence instead of repeatedly sending the same unexplained screenshot. Where support communicates a decision, save the wording and check which next steps it offers. The aim is a traceable outcome based on the parcel record, not an assumed resolution derived from the word delivered or from another shopper's experience.
